items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: There’s a lot of composers that I really admire, you know Duke Ellington and Monk especially. And I’m often inspired by one of their tunes.

ctx.x: Where do you get inspiration from for your original compositions?

A lot of different places. Other people’s tunes, something I hear somebody say in the street sometimes or bird calls. Sometimes I’m just sitting at the piano and I come up with a bass line that’s kind of cool and I say this could be something. So I make a voice memo of it. And maybe nothing happens but maybe a week later I listen to it and I say yeah, that was a cool idea, how about this? I’ll add a couple of chords here and sometimes a tune is built that way. Sometimes I write lyrics. Don’t ask me to sing them…

Oh yes. Have you ever had — this is sort of a change of subject — but have you ever been at like a high school jazz gathering of big bands and watched the drummer, who is so concerned with playing every possible thing written in his drum part?
